reason: The young Sun and its disk seem like a useful starting point for understanding the temperature differences behind both goals.
expectation: I expect the Sun to heat the disk unevenly, though I am unsure what this combination will produce.

effect: The result confirms that sunlight and accretion create a hotter inner disk, making temperature relevant to which materials stay solid.
reaction: The distinction between heating by sunlight and accretion is interesting.
reason: Following the hot disk into inner orbits seems like a direct way to develop the rocky-material goal.
expectation: I expect a more defined inner-disk region or heated material, though the exact result is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy dust could show what happens to water near the Sun, but I want to follow the disk conditions first.

effect: The hottest inner disk vaporizes inherited grains, so rocky material must be reprocessed before it can form solids again.
reaction: It is interesting that older stardust can be completely reworked.
reason: Combining the vapor with open space may let it cool and move toward forming rocky material.
expectation: I expect the vapor to cool, perhaps allowing solids to condense, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy dust could explain water's fate in inner orbits, but I want to follow the vapor first.

effect: Cooling the vapor produced refractory grains, providing a component for the inner disk’s rocky mixture.
reaction: The contrast between high-temperature mineral condensation and ice preservation is useful.
reason: Combining the new mineral grains with rock-forming dust directly advances the rocky-mixture goal.
expectation: I expect a mixed rocky material, though it may need further processing.

alternatives.reason: I also considered following the ice into hot orbits, but want to finish the rocky mixture first.

effect: The grains now form a loose aggregate, but the rocky-mixture goal has not yet completed.

reason: Brief heating may further process the aggregate toward the rocky-mixture goal.
expectation: I expect the aggregate to be heated or partially melted, though the exact result is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy dust could advance the water story, but I want to follow the aggregate first.

effect: Brief heating melted some solids into droplets; cooling them seems the next step toward the rocky mixture.
reaction: Leaving the disputed heating mechanism open is a useful clarification.
reason: Open space may allow the molten droplets to cool and solidify.
expectation: I expect solid rocky droplets to form, though I am unsure what they will be called.

alternatives.reason: I considered following the ice into hot orbits, but want to finish processing the droplets first.

effect: The droplets cooled into chondrules, which can now be combined with metal grains for the rocky mixture.
reaction: Their textures preserving evidence of rapid heating and cooling are interesting.
reason: Combining chondrules with metal grains seems a direct way to complete the inner-disk mixture.
expectation: I expect a rocky mixture containing chondrules and metal, though it may need another step.

reaction: The distinction between assembled ingredients and an actual planet is helpful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should begin the remaining ice pathway.
expectation: I expect the ice to vaporize in the hot inner orbits, though I am unsure how it will reach the colder region afterward.

effect: Ice sublimates in warm orbits, leaving water vapor that can now be paired with colder outer orbits.
reaction: It is useful to see that the water remains present even when the ice disappears.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the goal of storing ice beyond the snow line.
expectation: I expect the water vapor to cool and form ice in the outer disk, though the exact result is uncertain.

reason: This is the only offered combination and should gather the recondensed ice with icy dust.

effect: The outer-disk store combines inherited and reprocessed ice with dust, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the two histories of the ice come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the heated droplets into cooled chondrules was worthwhile: their textures preserve evidence of rapid heating and cooling, while the cause of heating remains uncertain.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final sequence felt somewhat repetitive because each decision offered only one combination, even though it clearly followed the water's changing state.

surprise.text: Inherited grains can evaporate in the hottest inner disk and later recondense as high-temperature minerals.

arbitrary.text: Combining hot vapor with open space to cool it felt somewhat abstract, though the resulting condensation had a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the stone, metal and ice become larger bodies, although I would hope for more meaningful choices than the final sequence offered.
